title: THE FIFTH PLAGUE AND A CLOSED HEART

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And the next day the Lord did it: All the livestock of the Egyptians died, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites died. Pharaoh investigated and found that not even one of the animals of the Israelites had died. Yet his heart was unyielding and he would not let the people go." - Exodus 9:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh does something interesting here. He investigates. He sends people to Goshen to check whether Israel's animals really survived.

He wanted evidence. He got it. Not one animal had died. The report came back exactly as God had said.

And then — yet his heart was unyielding.

This is a striking picture of how unbelief actually works. Pharaoh was not short of information. He conducted his own inquiry and confirmed the miracle personally. It changed nothing.

We often assume that if someone doubts, they simply need more proof. Sometimes that is true, and honest questions deserve honest answers. But Pharaoh reminds us that a heart set against God can absorb any amount of evidence and remain unmoved.

That is why Scripture speaks of God giving us new hearts (Ezek 36:26), not merely new information. Only God can change what evidence cannot reach.

Pray for hearts. Then keep loving people while you wait.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I asked God for proof when what I really need is a softer heart?
2. Am I praying for the people I long to see believe, or only arguing with them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, only You can change a heart. Soften mine, and work in those I love who cannot yet see You. Amen.
